insight.title: Why Being Too Efficient Makes You Fragile
insight.subtitle: How cutting out every extra step makes your system easy to break

sections.text: We spend our lives trying to delete "waste" from our digital workflows. But nature is intentionally wasteful. You have two kidneys not for performance, but to ensure a single injury isn't fatal.

We incorrectly apply machine-like efficiency to our software and habits. We strip away every redundant step to save seconds, but this creates a system where one minor glitch can break your entire day.

A forest thrives because it is redundant, not because it is lean. When you prioritize pure speed over safety margins, you aren't becoming more productive; you are simply making your success more precarious.
Try this today: When you open an app today, identify one backup way to finish that same task.
Resilience is the ability to be wrong without being ruined.
